questions.q: At $783 \mathrm{~K}$ in the reaction $\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{I}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$, the molar concentrations $\left(\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right.$ ) of $\mathrm{H}_{2}, \mathrm{I}_{2}$ and HI at some instant of time are $0.1,0.2$ and $0.4$, respectively. If the equilibrium constant is 46 at the same temperature, then as the reaction proceeds
options: the amount of HI will increase
the amount of HI will decrease
the amount of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ will increase
the amount of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ will not change
questions.solution:
Reaction quotient
$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{Q}=\frac{[\mathrm{HI}]^{2}}{\left[\mathrm{H}_{2}\right]\left[\mathrm{I}_{2}\right]}=\frac{0.4 \times 0.4}{0.1 \times 0.2} \\
\mathrm{Q}=8 \\
\mathrm{Q} \lt  \mathrm{K}
\end{array}$
So reaction will proceeds in forward direction. 
Hence amount of HI increases.

questions.q: Among (i) $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{3}$, (ii) $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{2}$, (iii) $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{3}$, (iv) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ the complex which is diamagnetic is
questions.solution:
(i) $\mathrm{Co}^{+3}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6} \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is a strong field ligand
(ii) $\mathrm{Ni}^{+2}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{8} 4 \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is a strong field ligand
(iii) $\mathrm{Cr}^{+3}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{3} 4 \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand
(iv) $\mathrm{Fe}^{+2}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6} 4 \mathrm{~s}^{0}\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand.
So, $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_{3}$ will be diamagnetic.

questions.q: The diameter of one of the bases of a truncated cone is $100 \mathrm{~mm}$. If the diameter of this base is increased by $21 \%$ such that it still remains a truncated cone with the height and the other base unchanged, the volume also increases by $21 \%$. The radius of the other base (in $\mathrm{mm}$ ) is-
questions.solution:
Let initially 2 bases have radii $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $\mathrm{r} \mathrm{cm}$. Finally base have radii $(1.21 \times 5)$ and $\mathrm{r}$.
Ratios of volumes $=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=1.21\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{V}_{2}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{h}}{3}\left[(6.05)^{2}+(6.05) \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{r}^{2}\right] \\
\mathrm{V}_{1}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{h}}{3}\left[5^{2}+5 \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{r}^{2}\right] \\
\frac{\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{~V}_{1}}=1.21 \Rightarrow \frac{(6.05)^{2}+(6.05) \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{r}^{2}}{5^{2}+5 \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{r}^{2}}=1.21 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}^{2}=\frac{6.3525}{21} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=\frac{11}{2} \mathrm{~cm}=55 \mathrm{~mm}
\end{array}$

questions.q: Let $f(x)=a x^{2}+b x+c$, where $a, b, c$ are integers. Suppose $f(1)=0,40 \lt  f(6) \lt  50,60 \lt  f(7) \lt  70$, and $1000 \mathrm{t} \lt  \mathrm{f}(50) \lt  1000(\mathrm{t}+1)$ for some integer $\mathrm{t}$. Then the value of $\mathrm{t}$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{ax}^{2}+\mathrm{bx}+\mathrm{c} \\
\text { given } \mathrm{f}(1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=0 \\
\text { and } 40 \lt  \mathrm{f}(6) \lt  50 \\
\Rightarrow 40 \lt  36 \mathrm{a}+6 \mathrm{~b}+\mathrm{c} \lt  50 \\
\Rightarrow 40 \lt  35 \mathrm{a}+5 \mathrm{~b} \lt  50 \\
\Rightarrow 8 \lt  7 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \lt  10 \\
7 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=\text { integer }=9 \\
\text { and } 60 \lt  \mathrm{f}(7) \lt  70 \\
\Rightarrow 60 \lt  49 \mathrm{a}+7 \mathrm{~b}+\mathrm{c} \lt  70 \\
\Rightarrow 60 \lt  48 \mathrm{a}+6 \mathrm{~b} \lt  70 \\
\Rightarrow 10 \lt  8 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \lt  11.6 \\
8 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=\text { integer }=11
\end{array}
Solving $(1) \&(2)\begin{array}{l}
a=2, b=-5, c=3 \\
\therefore \quad f(x)=2 x^{2}-5 x+3 \\
\quad f(50)=4753 \\
1000 t < f(50) < 1000(t+1) \\
(1000 \times 4) < 4753 < 1000(4+1) \\
\therefore \quad t=4
\end{array}

questions.q: In a thermally isolated system, two boxes filled with an ideal gas are connected by a valve. When the valve is in closed position, states of the box 1 and 2 , respectively, are (1 atm, V, T) and (0.5 atm, $4 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{~T}$ ). questions.solution: After opening of at equilibrium temperature and pressure of whole gas is $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{1}\begin{array}{l} n_{1}=\frac{1 \times V}{R T}, n_{2}=\frac{0.5 \times V \times 4}{R T} \\ n_{1}+n_{2}=n \\ \frac{V}{R T}+\frac{V \times 4}{2 R T}=\frac{5 V P_{1}}{R T_{1}} \\ \frac{3 V}{R T}=\frac{5 V P_{1}}{R T_{1}} \\ \frac{P_{1}}{T_{1}}=\frac{0.6}{T} \\ \Delta Q=0, \quad \Delta W=0 \\ \therefore \Delta U=0 \\ n_{1} C_{V} T+n_{2} C_{V} T=\left(n_{1}+n_{2}\right) C_{V} T_{1} \\ T_{1}=T \\ \frac{P_{1}}{T}=\frac{0.6}{T} \\ P_{1}=0.6 \text { atm } \end{array}$
